# M2: NeuroLab

Branch `feat/m2-neurolab`, worktree `../nt-m2`. Read `STATUS.md` first. **No API or database
changes in this milestone.** Everything is TypeScript, content and UI.

## Goal

NeuroLab makes the neuroscience of reward and addiction something you can explore:
- A 3D brain explorer.
- Region pages built on verified references.
- An interactive reward-learning simulator built on established models.

All of it is educational. The models are abstract learning models and **never claim to simulate
dopamine concentrations**.

## Checklist

### Content (`src/lib/content/brain-regions.ts`)
- [x] Typed `BrainRegion` entries (slug, name, abbreviation, anatomical description, primary
      functions, relationship to reward and learning, relevance to addiction research,
      `references[]`, and a 3D position and colour for the explorer) for: prefrontal cortex,
      amygdala, nucleus accumbens, basal ganglia (dorsal striatum focus), hippocampus, ventral
      tegmental area.
- [x] 2–4 references per region, chosen from well-known reviews (for example Koob & Volkow;
      Schultz; Everitt & Robbins; Hyman, Malenka & Nestler). **Resolve every DOI through Crossref
      before you add it.** Store the DOI, plus the PMID when you can resolve one through E-utilities.
      Write copy that is accurate, measured and sourced. If you are unsure of a claim, leave it out.
- [x] A Jest test that checks every region has at least 2 references, each with a DOI matching
      `^10\.\d{4,9}/`, and that slugs are unique.

### 3D brain explorer (`/neuro`)
- [ ] Replace the `ComingSoon` page.
- [ ] Build a React Three Fiber canvas, loaded with `next/dynamic` and `ssr: false`, containing a
      stylised translucent brain: two hemisphere ellipsoids plus a brainstem or cerebellum hint.
      **No external model files.**
- [ ] Place the 6 regions as selectable glowing meshes at approximate anatomical positions.
- [ ] Add OrbitControls, hover highlight and click-to-select. The selected region opens a side
      panel with a summary and a link to its region page.
- [ ] Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: no auto-rotate when it is set.
- [ ] Accessibility: add a keyboard-usable region list beside the canvas (buttons) that controls
      the same selection, and give the canvas an `aria-label`.
- [ ] Fallback: if WebGL is unavailable, show the region list only.
- [ ] Make the layout work at phone width.

### Region pages (`/neuro/regions/[slug]`)
- [x] Use `generateStaticParams` over the content. Show every field and a references list that
      links to `https://doi.org/<doi>` (and PubMed when there is a PMID).
- [x] Unknown slug → `notFound()`.

### Reward-learning simulator (`/neuro/reward-learning`)
- [x] `src/lib/models/rescorla-wagner.ts`: `ΔV = αβ(λ − V)`, with cue salience α, learning rate
      β, and reward magnitude λ (0 during extinction trials). Inputs: trials, acquisition and
      extinction phases, and an optional reward probability with a seeded PRNG (mulberry32), so
      results are deterministic.
- [x] `src/lib/models/td-learning.ts`: TD(0) over a short trial (cue → delay steps → reward).
      Return the value per state and the prediction error δ per trial. Show the textbook result:
      δ moves from reward time to cue time as learning proceeds.
- [ ] Add a "stress" parameter, documented clearly as a **hypothetical modulation** (for example,
      scaling reward sensitivity or learning rate). Label it as such in the UI and the model
      card. It must not be presented as an empirical relationship.
- [x] Jest tests:
  - Rescorla-Wagner converges to λ.
  - α or β = 0 means no learning.
  - Extinction decays V towards 0.
  - Seeded runs are deterministic.
  - In TD, δ at the cue grows and δ at the reward shrinks over trials.
  - Inputs are validated (clamped, or rejected by a zod schema).
- [x] UI:
  - Sliders, presets ("acquisition", "extinction", "partial reinforcement") and an explainer.
  - Recharts for V over trials and δ over trials.
  - A TD heat-strip or line chart that shows δ shifting.
  - Recompute in the browser instantly; no server round-trip.
- [x] Saving a run to `experiments` (module `neuro`) is optional, through a Server Action that
      uses `src/lib/experiments.ts`.

### Docs and tests
- [ ] Model cards `docs/models/rescorla-wagner.md` and `docs/models/td-learning.md`. Each has
      purpose, equations, parameters, assumptions, limitations and verified references (Rescorla
      & Wagner 1972 is a book chapter; cite it as such without a DOI, and use DOIs only for
      journal articles; Sutton 1988; Schultz, Dayan & Montague 1997).
- [ ] A Playwright spec `e2e/neurolab.spec.ts` covering both pages. Gate the signed-in parts on
      `E2E_USER_EMAIL`, like `e2e/quantum.spec.ts`. Do not run it.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` are green.
